title: Doping-driven Mott transition from steady-state density functional theory
abstract: The doping-driven Mott transition in the Hubbard model is described within the frame- work of steady-state density functional theory, or i-DFT. In order to access the many-body spectral function in i-DFT, an approximation for the exchange-correlation (xc) bias at arbitrary density and current is required. By using Fermi-liquid theory, a connection between the xc bias of i-DFT and the quasiparticle weight of many-body theory is derived and the results are employed to guide the construction of the approximation. Numerical results obtained with this functional demonstrate that the doping-driven Mott transition can indeed be captured with i-DFT.
summary: This work develops and applies a specialized version of Density Functional Theory (i-DFT) to model the Mott metal-insulator transition in the Hubbard model. By connecting the theory to many-body concepts like the quasiparticle weight, the authors show that i-DFT can accurately predict the opening and closing of the Mott gap as the electron doping changes. This advances the theoretical understanding of strongly correlated materials using non-equilibrium quantum methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of theoretically describing the doping-driven Mott transition, a fundamental phase transition driven by strong electronic interactions.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate that the doping-driven Mott transition in the Hubbard model can be captured using the steady-state density functional theory (i-DFT) framework.
method: The core method involves extending DFT to steady-state conditions (i-DFT) and deriving necessary approximations for the exchange-correlation (xc) bias by connecting it to the quasiparticle weight via Fermi-liquid theory.
model_or_system: The study uses the single-band Hubbard model, analyzed in the limit of infinite coordination (Bethe lattice), which allows mapping to a local Anderson Impurity Model (AIM) central to DMFT.
key_observables: Spectral function A(omega), Mott gap, quasiparticle weight, and the xc bias.
important_parameters: Interaction strength U, doping level (n), and the critical gate voltage (vc).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the validity of connecting the xc bias to the quasiparticle weight via Fermi-liquid theory, and it relies on the infinite coordination limit ($K 	o \infty$).
figures_summary: Figures compare the spectral function in metallic and Mott regimes, showing the emergence and disappearance of quasiparticle peaks and the opening/closing of the Mott gap as doping changes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the i-DFT formalism, parametrizes the Hxc potential using constraints from DMFT/NRG, and then applies the full framework to calculate the spectral function and diagnose the Mott transition across varying doping levels.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the development of a functional theory (i-DFT) that bridges equilibrium DFT with non-equilibrium transport and strong correlations is a powerful methodological tool applicable to open quantum systems where current/bias effects are crucial.
